title: Data Center Strategic Sourcing Lead - Construction
location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are hiring a Construction Sourcing Manager to develop and execute procurement strategies for the materials, components, and parts needed to build Anthropic's data centers. In this role, you will own end-to-end sourcing for construction materials such as wire and cable, lugs and connectors, conduit and cable tray, breakers and fuses, grounding, pipe, valves, fittings, and structural supports. You will partner closely with engineering, construction, demand planning, general contractors, and trade contractors to make sure the right material is on site when crews need it, establish direct manufacturer and distributor relationships, and negotiate commercial agreements. This role complements our major equipment sourcing leads: they source the equipment, and you source what is needed to install, connect, and energize it. Key responsibilities Own sourcing for electrical construction materials: medium- and low-voltage cable, building wire, control and instrumentation cable, lugs, connectors, terminations and splice kits, conduit and fittings, cable tray, busway, breakers, fuses, panelboards, grounding, and enclosures. Own sourcing for mechanical and structural construction materials: pipe, valves, fittings, flanges, gaskets, hoses, insulation, sensors, strut, hangers, anchors, and fasteners. Negotiate Master Purchase Agreements, national pricing agreements, and blanket orders with manufacturers and distributors, including index-based pricing for copper, aluminum, and steel, capacity reservations, and volume rebates. Run competitive RFQs, build should-cost models and unit-price benchmarks, and audit contractor material pricing, markups, and procurement schedules. Decide with construction and design partners which materials to buy direct versus through contractors, and aggregate demand across sites to secure better price and supply. Implement frameworks for ensuring data center partners, general contractors, and trade contractors buy against our negotiated terms, approved manufacturer lists, and technical specifications. Work with engineering to standardize parts, qualify second sources, and approve alternates that meet code, listing (e.g., NEC, UL), and design requirements. Develop material inventory and logistics strategy including distributor stocking programs, buffer stock, cable cutting and reel management, kitting, staging, and just-in-time site delivery. Proactively monitor supply chain volatility (e.g., commodity prices, tariffs, and lead times for medium-voltage cable, breakers, and valves), expedite shortages, and execute contingency plans to avoid project delays. Translate drawings, bills of materials, quantity takeoffs, and construction schedules into material forecasts and procurement pipelines, and update them as designs change. Partner with Finance on material budgets, commodity exposure, inventory investment, and savings tracking. Establish efficient workflows for damaged, defective, short-shipped, and surplus material, including returns and redeployment across sites. Negotiate warranty, delivery, and spare parts terms, and track supplier performance on on-time delivery, fill rate, quality, and price. Minimum qualifications Have 7+ years experience in sourcing, procurement, or supply chain management, including direct experience buying electrical or mechanical construction materials. Have a track record of forecasting, sourcing, and delivering high-volume, multi-SKU construction materials against active project schedules. Have negotiated supply agreements with both manufacturers and electrical or mechanical distributors, and understand commodity-linked pricing. Are familiar with data center construction materials (e.g., MV/LV cable, lugs, terminations, conduit, cable tray, busway, breakers, grounding, pipe, valves, fittings, supports) and can read drawings, specifications, and bills of materials. Possess a bachelor's degree in a relevant domain (e.g., electrical/mechanical engineering, construction management, supply chain) or equivalent practical experience. Preferred qualifications 10+ years experience in construction sourcing, procurement, or supply chain management. 5+ years experience in data center, semiconductor, energy, or other large industrial construction programs. Experience working for or with electrical or mechanical contractors, general contractors, distributors, or prefabrication and modular integrators. Experience setting up owner-furnished or direct-purchase material programs across multiple sites. Familiarity with liquid cooling piping materials (stainless pipe, quick disconnects, manifolds, hoses) and medium-voltage terminations. Leadership and influencing skills. Deadline to apply: None.
